compliments: The work shows great investment and creativity, with a strong cultural motif and cohesive visual language.
The layout design demonstrates excellent use of symbolic imagery—bamboo, the Vietnamese map, and stars—to reinforce national identity.
The color palette is warm and harmonious, effectively using greens and golds to evoke nature, growth, and prosperity.

e.r: Multiple competing focal points: the top banner, the four numbered panels, and the repeated logo create visual fragmentation instead of a single dominant hierarchy. <box>(0,0),(998,348)</box><box>(0,350),(998,990)</box>
e.issue: The composition lacks a single primary focal point; the large title 'VIỆT ĐỒNG TÂM' competes with the four-panel grid, and each panel has its own internal focal point (icon + number), resulting in visual clutter and no clear entry point for the viewer.
e.suggestion: Establish a clear visual hierarchy by either elevating the main title with a stronger contrast or repositioning the four-panel grid to serve as the primary structure, with the title as a header only.
e.rule_violated: [Poster Design > I. Elements and Getting Attention] — A single focal point is required

e.r: The background texture (circular seal patterns) bleeds into the foreground elements, reducing figure-ground contrast and making text and icons hard to read. <box>(0,350),(998,990)</box>
e.issue: The background features faint circular seal patterns that are too prominent, competing with the foreground content for attention and violating the rule that ground must not dominate figure. This reduces legibility of both text and icons in the four panels.
e.suggestion: Reduce the opacity or desaturate the background pattern to below 20% so it functions as a subtle texture without interfering with readability.
e.rule_violated: [Poster Design > Composition and Spatial Structure] — Figure-ground must be clear at a glance

e.r: Inconsistent typography across panels: different font weights, sizes, and spacing for similar information (e.g., 'Challenge:' vs. 'Dấu Ấn Trăm') cause confusion and break campaign continuity. <box>(150,370),(498,560)</box><box>(500,370),(848,560)</box><box>(150,680),(498,870)</box><box>(500,680),(848,870)</box>
e.issue: The typographic system is inconsistent: 'NHÂN THỨC BÌNH DẲNG' uses bold serif, while 'KHỞI DẬY DOANH KẾT' uses bold sans-serif; 'Challenge:' and 'Dấu Ấn Trăm' vary in size and weight across panels, undermining the perception of a unified series.
e.suggestion: Standardize the typographic system: define one heading font (e.g., bold sans-serif), one subheading font (e.g., medium sans-serif), and one body font (e.g., regular sans-serif) with fixed weights and sizes across all panels.
e.rule_violated: [Poster Design > IV. Pattern, Rhythm, and Campaign Continuity] — Continuity connects campaign materials across time and space

e.r: The bamboo icon in the top-right corner overlaps with the star and map, creating visual conflict and breaking the clarity of the logo’s symbolic meaning. <box>(698,45),(958,250)</box>
e.issue: The stylized bamboo graphic in the top-right corner partially obscures the yellow star and the red Vietnam map, causing visual tension and weakening the integrity of the core brand symbol.
e.suggestion: Reposition or scale down the bamboo element so it frames rather than overlaps the star and map, preserving the symbolic clarity of the logo.
e.rule_violated: [Logo Design > III. Graphic Identity as a System] — The logo is the anchor of a graphic identity system

e.r: The 'TÁC GIẢ', 'VIỆT ĐỒNG TÂM Team', and 'TRÒ CHƠI' icons in the left column are misaligned vertically and lack consistent sizing, disrupting rhythm and balance. <box>(20,450),(100,640)</box>
e.issue: The three small circular icons on the left side of the first panel are inconsistently sized and spaced, breaking the visual rhythm and failing to form a coherent vertical list.
e.suggestion: Align all icons to a common grid, ensure uniform diameter (e.g., 40px), and apply consistent vertical spacing (e.g., 10px padding) to establish rhythmic consistency.
e.rule_violated: [Layout Design > Layout and Spatial Structure] — Alignment and Grid Consistency Rule
